concepts.definition: Specification-driven development is a governed derivation and disambiguation method: current goals precede deeper repricing, intent precedes implementation, product definition precedes detailed requirements, and design explicitly bridges requirements to code.

grounding.quote:
The method commits to these (P2, P6). It defines the
current goals for the active body of work before repricing deeper
constitutional layers. It works from intent before implementation. It
defines the current product definition in explicit present-tense terms
before decomposing it into detailed requirements. It defines the full
constitutional what in requirements, not merely a feature list. It prefers
declaring desired truth and lawful boundaries over prescribing step-by-step
imperative procedure. It makes design the explicit structural bridge
between requirements and code. It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent. It treats
spec-driven development as a disambiguation pipeline: each major gate
reduces the space of lawful interpretations before downstream realisation
proceeds.

concepts.label: Specification-driven method

concepts.definition: Goals orient the current bounded work wave; they do not substitute for requirements.

grounding.quote:
Goals orient the current bounded work
wave and are not a substitute requirement surface.

concepts.label: Goals surface

concepts.definition: Intent states why the system exists and which directional change is in or out of scope.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope; it carries
no optional realisation detail unless that detail is itself constitutional.

concepts.label: Intent surface

concepts.definition: Product definition is the current concrete, present-tense bridge from intent to requirements, including lifecycle signal material to product meaning; it is not release notes.

grounding.quote:
Product states the current concrete product definition and bridges intent
to requirements; it is not a release-note surface; it carries enough
operational lifecycle signal for downstream requirements and design to
understand intended use, release and install posture, live-use posture,
observability posture, and retirement or supersession posture where those
materially affect product meaning.

concepts.label: Product definition

concepts.definition: Requirements state the full constitutional WHAT as stable obligations with explicit acceptance criteria, sufficient for downstream design derivation.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state stable obligations
that must be true; they carry explicit acceptance criteria and remain
sufficient for downstream design derivation, including lifecycle
obligations or named lifecycle ambiguity gaps where build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, telemetry or retirement materially affect
the obligation.

concepts.label: Requirements surface

concepts.definition: Design is the downstream structural HOW that realises requirement truth and chooses lawful mechanisms, structures, interfaces, carriers, packaging and tenant boundaries.

grounding.quote:
Design states how requirement truth is realised; it is
downstream of requirements and may choose structure, interfaces, carriers,
packaging and tenant boundaries. ADRs are durable design memory, not a
second requirement surface.

concepts.label: Design surface

concepts.definition: Code is executable realisation derived from requirements and design, rather than a source of authority through accidental precedent.

grounding.quote:
It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent.

concepts.label: Code realisation

concepts.definition: Reconstruction sufficiency is competent reconstruction of conformant downstream layers in order. It is not determinism and cannot depend on hiding major ambiguity.

grounding.quote:
The generic law, that a layered specification is sufficient when a competent
actor can derive each layer from the one above, that sufficiency is not
determinism, that a boundary crossed only by hiding a major ambiguity is not
sufficient, and that an accepted relation may be reused on its exact basis
after checking applicability and invalidation, is EVALUATION §6.

concepts.label: Reconstruction sufficiency

concepts.definition: Renewal is the cumulative feedback cycle from current specification through real-world use case and explicit gap analysis to lawful re-entry and forward repricing.

grounding.quote: current specification → real-world use case → gap analysis → re-entry at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Renewal cycle

conditions: The tier-3 DESIGN_MODULE profile governs the boundary under its own adoption rule.
concepts.definition: The design profile's realisation shape makes meaning readable as transforms over admitted truth and locates effects explicitly at the edge.

grounding.quote:
For a realisation boundary that the design profile governs (DESIGN_MODULE,
tier 3, adopted under its own adoption rule), the core rule is: semantic
steps should read as transforms over admitted truth; effects should be
explicit and pushed to the edge. If a reader has to inspect orchestration
code, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults to
determine what the system means, the design is too imperative and too
coupled (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Profile-governed realisation shape

concepts.definition: Requirement category and lifecycle status are independent declared-state domains. Categories are Capability (required behaviour/function/surface), Constraint / Guarantee (invariant, law, safety, portability or semantic bound), Governance (lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator policy), and Verification (tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic obligations). Statuses are Active, Deferred, Superseded and Orphaned.

grounding.quote:
| Capability | a behaviour, function or surface the system must provide | what can the system do |
| Constraint / Guarantee | an invariant, law, safety property, portability rule or semantic guarantee that bounds how the system may behave | what must always remain true |
| Governance | a policy or control rule over lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator action | what governs use and change |
| Verification | a requirement on tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic surfaces | how do we know the claim is true |

Every live requirement family is classified on two independent axes (P3,
P1): lifecycle status (Active,
Deferred, Superseded, Orphaned) and requirement category (the four above).

concepts.label: Requirement classifications

concepts.definition: Constitutional trace closure closes the constitution over realised behaviour and is stricter than documentation completeness.

grounding.quote:
Spec-driven development requires constitutional trace closure: the rule
that closes the constitution over realised behaviour, stricter than
documentation completeness (P6, P4b).

concepts.label: Constitutional trace closure

conditions: A domain artifact has been published as a live constitutional surface.
concepts.definition: A live domain surface is versioned constitutional history, immutable in place; a project may accumulate multiple such surfaces.

grounding.quote:
A project may accumulate multiple live domain surfaces over time. A live
surface is versioned constitutional history, not scratch space (P3). Engine code, design documents, tests and
tooling may be refactored aggressively while they remain mutable
implementation surfaces. Live domain artifacts, once published as live
constitutional surfaces, are immutable in place; if one is wrong, the valid
actions are to supersede it with a new version or to withdraw or delete it

concepts.label: Live domain surface

conditions: The designed product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface or capability is material.
concepts.definition: The canonical operational lifecycle is intent, requirement, build, assurance, release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry and retirement. A phase has one declared answer: answered; not applicable with reason; or a named Gap:/Unanswered: marker.

grounding.quote:
Any material
product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin
surface, public interface, data surface or capability has an operational
lifecycle, whose canonical chain is intent, requirement, build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement.

Each phase has one of three answers, and this
section owns them: the phase is answered by the surface; if a phase is
not applicable, the surface says why; if it is unknown, a named gap such
as `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` is recorded.
Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.

concepts.label: Operational lifecycle

conditions: The work wave bears a product outcome.
concepts.definition: A work wave binds one explicitly selected, unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome instance and its declared acceptance interval.

grounding.quote:
Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected,
unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and declares the
acceptance interval for that instance. Product-progress claims and
promotion onto the supported product path are judged against that same
outcome (P2; FOUNDATIONS §2
Outcome U is the generic object).

concepts.label: Selected product outcome

concepts.definition: Product-outcome evidence distinguishes material advance, prerequisite readiness, preservation and regression. These are declared classifications rather than evaluation core values.

grounding.quote:
Evidence distinguishes material advance, prerequisite readiness,
preservation and regression. The four refine the progress
categories of [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)
(Progress) for a product outcome: material advance is progress there,
accepted material movement toward the selected product outcome, and only
material advance projects product progress; prerequisite readiness is
its prerequisite work, which names the product obligation it enables and
here also remains bounded; preservation is its preservation and repeated
proof, useful evidence, not progress; regression maps to evidence that
is not new progress, and this member adds one need to it: the promotion
block in the last paragraph of this section. Churn and the revision of the forecast are
ACTIVATION §5's, unchanged here.

concepts.label: Outcome evidence classes

conditions: Within a product-outcome-bearing work wave.
concepts.definition: Material growth has a live basis in the selected unresolved outcome, an admitted named bounded prerequisite, or an admitted named bounded experiment whose stated observation discriminates a stated decision for that outcome.

grounding.quote:
Within a product-outcome-bearing work wave, material realisation growth
derives its authority from the selected unresolved product outcome, an
admitted named bounded prerequisite to it, or an admitted named bounded
experiment whose stated observation discriminates a stated decision for it.
A prerequisite or experiment authorises only its declared provisional
bound; it does not select or enlarge the product outcome, authorise
downstream work, confer promotion or closure, or waive applicable design,
safety, authority or release law, including the prime law of a design
profile where one applies.

concepts.label: Bounded growth basis

concepts.definition: Change management routes reports through intake triage, owning-layer change classification, separation of computed treatment from judgment and owner decisions, and affected-span consistency closure.
concepts.label: Change management

concepts.definition: F11 is the foundation-to-law family accounting for change entry, computed classification and reuse, ambiguity governance and shared-interface migration. Its instance premises are changing specification, one front door, shared interfaces with multiple producers/consumers, and decisions either under declared policy or reserved to human authority. It reports P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; and P5 derived from P0/P6 with an open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
This family (F11 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides how a change enters the chain, how its classification is computed
and reused, how ambiguity is governed and how a shared interface is
migrated. Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are
named in the rows as follows: changing specification, the specification
changes while work proceeds; one front door, reports of every kind arrive
at one product; shared interfaces, a shared interface has several
producers and consumers; reserved decisions, a decision may be taken
under declared policy or be reserved to a human authority. Standing of
the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and
P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that
step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5 derived from P0 and P6,
with P0's open-world premise.

concepts.label: F11 foundation-to-law family

concepts.definition: Universal intake triage is the single entry for substantive change, determining substance, affected product boundary/scope, lawful class, re-entry point, affected downstream surfaces/evidence, and release-scope fit or repricing.

grounding.quote:
Intake triage determines six things: whether the report represents a
substantive change at all; the affected product boundary and intended
scope; the lawful change class; the lawful re-entry point into the
constitutional chain; the downstream surfaces and evidence that must be
repriced, re-derived or re-proved, a determination whose evidence part is
the selection `S_Δ` over the impact cover `I(Δ)` of the affected surfaces
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse));
and whether the work remains within the
currently declared release scope or requires repricing of that release
plan.

concepts.label: Universal intake triage

concepts.definition: The minimum lawful declared change classes are goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe and realization_refactor. Each identifies changed meaning, lawful re-entry and downstream flow; a declared class is not an evaluation result.

grounding.quote:
| `goal_reprice` | current bounded work-wave focus changes | Goals | Intent, Product, Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence where that focus changes deeper constitutional truth |
| `intent_reprice` | directional or scope change | Intent | Product, Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence |
| `product_reprice` | current product realisation changes while directional intent stays stable | Product | Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence |
| `requirement_reprice` | constitutional truth changes while project direction stays stable | Requirements | Design, Code, Evidence |
| `design_reframe` | realisation structure changes while active intent and requirement truth stay stable | Design | Code, Evidence |
| `realization_refactor` | local code, configuration or attribute change with no intended constitutional or structural change | the realised surface only | nothing upstream; it must prove no upstream drift |

concepts.label: Change classes

concepts.definition: Reusable intake classification distinguishes C, reproducible facts and declared-rule application; J, residual semantic/materiality judgment; and O, a ruling reserved to its actual owner. These annotations create no authority, calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory document.

grounding.quote:
Intake supplies one reusable classification result rather than requiring
each role to reconstruct the same facts (P4b, P6, P1). Three annotations keep the kinds
of determination apart: C denotes reproducible facts and declared rule
application; J denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment; O denotes
a ruling reserved to its actual owner. The annotations grant no authority,
an instance of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
creates no authority, and introduce no calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory
document.

concepts.label: Computed classification and C/J/O

concepts.definition: The consistency gate applies the externally owned condition-based closure rule to obligations of a declared change span, requiring upstream sufficiency, downstream consistency and evidence of active intended behaviour.

grounding.quote:
No gate closes while the affected active surfaces are internally
inconsistent (P6, P4b). For the declared
change span the framework proves that the upstream surface remains
sufficient for the downstream surface, that downstream artifacts do not
contradict active upstream truth, and that tests and qualification prove
the active intended behaviour rather than stale precedent. If that proof is
missing the change remains open even if one local artifact already looks
correct.

concepts.label: Consistency gate

concepts.definition: A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface under existing constitutional authority, allowing batching, coordination, proof-cost pricing and close review without becoming a constitutional layer.

grounding.quote:
A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface, not a new layer in the
constitutional chain (P6, P2). It may
batch work, coordinate tickets or iteration entries, price proof cost and
force close review under existing goals, intent, product definition,
requirements and design authority; it does not create, supersede, weaken
or override that authority.

concepts.label: Sprint execution boundary

concepts.definition: Work-carrier selection follows required lifetime: durable ticket for cross-session identity; sprint-local entry for within-batch traceability only; run/return record for one activation.

grounding.quote:
The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime: a
durable ticket where the work needs identity across sessions; a
sprint-local entry where its only value is traceability inside a batch; a
run or return record where the work lives and dies with one activation.

concepts.label: Work-carrier selection

concepts.definition: The method describes procedures for substantive intake, feature introduction/change, project bootstrap or requirement repricing, and use-case gaps. They preserve triage-first re-entry and downstream consistency.

grounding.quote:
When any substantive intake arrives (P2, P4b): enter
[Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage), keeping classification
unresolved until the evidence supports a lawful class; determine the lawful
re-entry point into the constitutional chain when that class is established; identify the affected downstream span that must
remain consistent; only then treat the work as implementation, repricing or
release-bound change.

concepts.label: Method procedures

concepts.definition: The substrate-neutral context urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance progressively narrows goals, direction/scope, product shape/terms, obligations, executable class, structure and local implementation. Major ambiguity materially affects architecture, stack, product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contracts or downstream law; micro ambiguity is local choice within an already-governed design boundary.

grounding.quote:
This member owns the substrate-neutral ambiguity-governance bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance` under the selected complete
basis; a profile's runtime shorthands for its own frames stay in that
profile's context unless an explicit relation imports or translates them
(P3, P1).

Major ambiguity materially changes
architecture, stack, product boundary, execution or deployment
admissibility, public contract shape or other downstream realisation law;
micro ambiguity is a local implementation choice inside an already-governed
design boundary.

concepts.label: Ambiguity governance

conditions: Declared policy permits bounded handling of declared ambiguity.
concepts.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing names bounded non-human processing permitted to carry or resolve declared ambiguity. The source also places a person's policy-permitted decision without human-adjudication admission under this processing's policy and recording rules.

grounding.quote:
Lawful probabilistic processing
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing`)
is bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or
resolve declared ambiguity.

concepts.label: Lawful probabilistic processing

conditions: Human judgment is explicitly admitted by authority where policy or risk appetite requires it.
concepts.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication names admitted human judgment resolving declared ambiguity. Admission, not the performer's identity or participation elsewhere, makes the operation human adjudication.

grounding.quote:
Human adjudication
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication`) is explicit
human judgment admitted by authority to resolve declared ambiguity where
policy or risk appetite requires it. That admission makes an operation
human adjudication. A person who relays, records or carries out a step
does not adjudicate by doing so, and a person who carries or decides a
declared ambiguity where policy permits it, without that admission, acts
under the policy and recording that govern lawful probabilistic
processing; who performs an operation does not decide its kind

concepts.label: Human adjudication

concepts.definition: Lineage distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. A release cut v<version>-rc.<n> is immutable point-in-time release identity; mutable v<version> is a discovery selector for the highest-ordinal published cut.

grounding.quote:
The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities,
substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product,
install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2
(product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler
analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense
surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be
running the build (P3).

The only exact operative release identifier is the immutable release-cut
tag `v<version>-rc.<n>` (P3). That cut is a
point-in-time release identity, a boundary over the feature set accepted
for that cut, and part of release metadata and release-process evaluation;
it is not part of the live project specification. The mutable `v<version>`
tag is a version-line discovery selector to the highest-ordinal published
immutable cut; it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional
basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection.

concepts.label: Lineage and release identities

conditions: A reusable change to the shared method is proposed.
concepts.definition: Shared-method adoption preserves authority causality from incident/review evidence through shared intake, one owning standard, consistency and independent review, human-authority acceptance, one complete released STDO version, explicit consumer selection, and consumer-owned realisation/evidence.

grounding.quote:
incident or review evidence
  -> shared-method intake
  -> one owning standard
  -> consistency and independent review
  -> human-authority acceptance
  -> one complete released STDO version
  -> explicit consumer selection
  -> consumer-owned realisation and evidence

concepts.label: Shared method adoption and propagation

concepts.definition: Migration is the document's section grouping for changes of constitutional or implementation basis.

grounding.quote: ## 7. Migration

concepts.label: Migration section

concepts.definition: A core interface is any shared contract/carrier materially governing runtime closure, reporting/status truth, topology/frame progression, proof/qualification, event/projection semantics, identity/binding resolution or provider/resolver behaviour. A change affecting how multiple surfaces decide current truth is a core-interface change.

grounding.quote:
A core interface is any shared contract or carrier that materially governs
runtime closure, reporting or status truth, topology or frame progression,
proof or qualification outcome, event or projection semantics, identity or
binding resolution, or provider or resolver behaviour. If changing the
interface can alter how multiple surfaces decide what is true now, it is a
core interface change (P3).

concepts.label: Core interface

conditions: A change alters a load-bearing shared contract, carrier, resolver, provider, projection law, closure law or other interface depended on by multiple surfaces.
concepts.definition: Constitutional migration replaces shared authority across the affected interface family; it is not ordinary incremental local patching.

grounding.quote:
Core interface changes are not ordinary local patches. Where a change
alters a load-bearing contract, carrier, resolver, provider, projection
law, closure law or other shared interface that multiple surfaces depend
on, the work is handled as a constitutional migration, not as incremental
patching (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Constitutional migration

concepts.definition: Two lawful strategies are inside-out hard-break migration on the same implementation line, replacing authoritative source truth from its carrier outward, and fundamental re-adoption for intentional major re-derivation on a materially different implementation basis. Bounded evolution is a rebuttable selection presumption, not a third strategy.

grounding.quote:
Core interface and major implementation replacement work has two lawful
constitutional strategies (P3, P6).
Inside-out hard-break migration applies when the project remains on the
same implementation line and the authoritative source truth is being
replaced in place; the work proceeds from the source carrier outward
through a sequence of deliberate breaks and repairs. Fundamental
re-adoption migration applies when the rewrite is major and the project is
intentionally re-deriving itself on a materially different implementation
basis, such as a new runtime model, carrier model, type system, execution
substrate or realisation tree; the prior implementation is moved sideways
and treated as reference material, not live authority.

concepts.label: Constitutional migration strategies

concepts.definition: An affected outcome's acceptance path is its full causal closure: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver, fallback, shared state, event, projection and proof surface capable of changing, interpreting or closing it.

grounding.quote:
For this rule the affected acceptance path is the full causal closure of
the outcome: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver,
fallback, shared state surface, event, projection and proof surface capable
of changing, interpreting or closing the outcome. Singular authority means
one governing authority across that closure, not one selected successful
trace. If the same request, fact, identity, state or projection is
admissible to old and new authority, authority is competing and promotion
blocks (P3).

concepts.label: Affected acceptance path

concepts.definition: Projections, reports, status views and topology views are downstream reflections of an authoritative carrier, not independent closure surfaces.

grounding.quote:
Projections, reports, status views and topology views may reflect the
authoritative carrier; they do not become a second closure surface (P6,
P1).

concepts.label: Projection read model

conditions: The project intentionally abandons its prior constitutional shape and re-derives on a new branch, version line or methodology basis.
concepts.definition: Fundamental migration is a constitutional reset through explicit adoption. Inherited constitutional material is classified adopted, superseded, deferred or orphaned; implementation is carry_across, redundant or rewrite.

grounding.quote:
A fundamental migration is a constitutional reset, not an in-place
refactor. It applies when a project intentionally abandons a prior
constitutional shape and re-derives itself on a new branch, version line or
methodology basis (P3, P6). In that case:
inherited constitutional documents from the prior line become migration
source material, not live authority in the new line; it is lawful to zero
inherited constitutional surfaces on the migration line and rebuild them
from first principles; nothing carries forward by default, and every
retained statement, requirement, design choice or guide rule must be

concepts.label: Fundamental migration

concepts.definition: A transformation wave describes refactor/migration over mutable implementation surfaces, with bounded non-authoritative transitional plumbing during the wave and one current operative surface for its affected scope when it lands.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable
implementation surfaces (P3, P6). While
the wave is in flight: temporary mixed-state implementation may exist only
below the current break boundary and only as explicitly non-authoritative
plumbing; transitional adapters or scaffolds may exist only when they are
named, bounded and outside the acceptance path; refactor state may still
carry traces of the prior operative model, never as competing or ambiguous
dual authority over the same request, fact, identity, state or projection.
Explicitly specified, deterministically routed, non-overlapping product or
compatibility scopes are not competing authority under this rule; they may
coexist while the enclosing migration remains visibly open.

concepts.label: Transformation wave

conditions: Construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker.
concepts.definition: The method applies ACTIVATION's bounded construction step: accepted basis, affected relation set, selected computations, delegated execution/decision authority, construction/self-review, independent assessment where required, owner disposition accept/local_repair/re_enter/reject, exact accepted checkpoint and next already-authorised action. Candidate availability, assessment and owner disposition are separate results.

grounding.quote:
Construction delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker is governed as
the step of ACTIVATION: the execution relation from accepted governing
basis through bounded affected relation set, selected computational
relations, delegated execution and decision authority, construction and
self-review, independent live-surface assessment where required, one of
accept, local repair, re-enter or reject, the exact accepted checkpoint,
and the next already-authorised bounded action (ACTIVATION §1, §3, §5 and
§7). The

concepts.label: Bounded execution

concepts.definition: Realisation evidence serves existing closure law with authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible and a present-tense statement of residual open pressure.

grounding.quote:
For a realisation claim, the evidence that the closure condition of
[TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse](TICKETS.md#condition-based-closure-and-reuse)
requires includes an authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof
where drift is plausible, and a present-tense statement of the residual
open pressure; this section adds no second closure condition (P6, P4b,
P5).

concepts.label: Realisation evidence

concepts.definition: An ADR is durable design memory per decision boundary: the choice making acceptance criteria true. Its declared statuses are active, superseded and retired; it is an authoritative design file, while templates and optional registries project its rules.

grounding.quote:
Each ADR explicitly includes `Status:` (`active`, `superseded` or
`retired`); `Implements:` (the requirement identifiers the ADR makes true);
`Derives from:` (the intent identifier or strategy document that motivated
the decision); `Supersedes:` (the prior ADR or doctrine it replaces);
`Superseded by:` (the successor ADR when its status is superseded); and
`Retained special case:` (when earlier behaviour is intentionally retained
as a special case of the current surface) (P6, P4b).
ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file; the
boundary is the question "what design choice makes these acceptance
criteria true".

concepts.label: Architecture decision record

concepts.definition: A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a product's WHAT, located by the product definition's tenant registry.

grounding.quote:
- A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT. The build-tenancy context of
  [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)
  names it, and the product definition's tenant registry locates each one.

concepts.label: Build tenant

concepts.definition: A product's requirements calculus comprises its WHAT obligations, permitted outcomes and rules for refining/composing realising work.

grounding.quote:
- The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.

concepts.label: Requirements calculus

concepts.definition: A computational calculus declares executable operations, composition laws, permitted transformations, effects and resource behaviour insofar as material to obligations.

grounding.quote:
- A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,
  with the laws by which they compose, the transformations they permit,
  and their effects and resource behaviour, as far as these are material
  to the obligations.

concepts.label: Computational calculus

concepts.definition: An execution environment performs operations through a technology stack, a human process comprising people/roles/documents/channels/decision procedures, or both.

grounding.quote:
- An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations: a technology stack; a human process, made of people, roles,
  documents, communication channels and decision procedures; or a
  combination of the two.

concepts.label: Execution environment

concepts.definition: Build-tenant binding comprises calculus binding from requirements calculus to computational calculus and execution binding from computational calculus to execution environment. A registry entry locates a tenant but is not its binding.

grounding.quote:
- A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts: its calculus binding,
  from the requirements calculus to its computational calculus, and its
  execution binding, from that computational calculus to its execution
  environment. A tenant's registry entry locates the tenant; it is not the
  binding.

concepts.label: Build-tenant binding

concepts.definition: TICKETS is the tier-2 owner of the work-carrier model, layout/bindings, sprint/ticket mechanics, triage/class recording/upward propagation, smallest lawful carrier and carrier-side execution-contract admission, execution/verification separation, judgment/ruling continuity, condition-based closure/reuse, test-case authority, migration-ticket rules, one-truth projection, recommended shapes and operating mode. It derives from FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION rather than establishing foundational law.

grounding.quote:
Tier 2. Owns the work carriers of the method: goals, tickets, sprints,
comments and execution contracts as one model; the default layout and the
bindings that locate the carriers; the sprint rules; the ticket rules,
including triage-first intake, the change class the ticket records and the
upward propagation check; the selection of the smallest lawful carrier for
a piece of work and the carrier side of execution-contract admission; the
separation of execution from verification authority; the continuity of
recorded judgment and owner rulings; condition-based closure and reuse;
test case authority; the implementation-migration ticket category with its
declaration, checklist and review rules; one-truth state projection; the
recommended ticket and sprint shape; the operating mode. It is realised
from [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md), [ACTIVATION](ACTIVATION.md) and
[EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md) and is the T area named by
[SPEC_METHOD §1](SPEC_METHOD.md#method-identity): nothing here is
foundational, every clause names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6,
FOUNDATIONS §3), and each mechanism could be realised differently under the

concepts.definition: In TICKETS, Goals is the current epic layer located by ticketing.goals, with GOALS.md as default. Broader than one ticket and narrower/more current than intent, it states the active wave and current priorities, not durable execution tracking.

grounding.quote:
The product definition's `ticketing.goals` binding locates the current epic
layer; `GOALS.md` is the default file (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §1). Goals are
broader than one ticket, narrower and more current than the intent surface,
and the place to state the active work wave and what matters now. Goals are
not the durable unit of execution tracking (P2, P3).

concepts.label: TICKETS goals carrier

conditions: Work needs independent durable identity, including feature work, bugs, spikes and chores.
concepts.definition: A ticket is one enduring, typed source-of-truth work record durable across sessions; one Markdown file is the default carrier and bugs/features share one system.

grounding.quote:
Tickets are the enduring work records. Each ticket is one durable record,
one markdown file being the default carrier; the source of truth for that
unit of work; durable across sessions; and typed, so that bugs and features
share one system. A ticket is used when work needs independent durable
identity: feature work, bug tracking, spikes and chores (P3, P4b).

concepts.label: Ticket record

concepts.definition: In TICKETS, a sprint is one bounded-batch manifest under optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/, batching authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and deferred local compliance debt and closing by explicit review.

grounding.quote:
Sprints are bounded execution batches. Each sprint is one manifest under
the product definition's optional `ticketing.sprints.root` binding,
`.ai-workspace/sprints/` being the default; a control surface for a bounded
body of work; a place to batch repeated authority references, closure law,
evidence expectations and deferred local compliance debt; and closed by an
explicit sprint-close review. Sprints are not constitutional authority: they
operate under SPEC_METHOD and the project surfaces they cite
([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#sprint-execution-boundary) states the
sprint boundary; this member states the mechanics) (P2, P6).

concepts.label: TICKETS sprint manifest

concepts.definition: Comments are POSTING_GUIDE posts for ideas, strategy, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries and reasoned decisions, located by ticketing.comments.root with .ai-workspace/comments/ as default. They have neither task-status authority nor independent decision authority.

grounding.quote:
The product definition's `ticketing.comments.root` binding is the message
board; `.ai-workspace/comments/` is the default. Comments are for publishing
ideas, strategy notes, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries, and decisions
with their reasoning. Comments are not task status authority. A comment
is a post of [POSTING_GUIDE](POSTING_GUIDE.md), which states what it
carries, its structure and its discussion state. A decision recorded in a
comment takes its authority from the surface that owns the decision, once
it is adopted there ([POSTING_GUIDE §9](POSTING_GUIDE.md#9-ratification)),
and has none of its own (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Comment carrier

exceptions: Transitional paths may remain as explicitly retained compatibility features.

grounding.quote:
It demands evidence for claims through scenarios, tests, events,
projection and delta. It treats repricing as part of correctness: when
reality exposes a constitutional gap, the specification changes. It keeps
authority directional while iterating: goals govern intent, intent governs
product definition, product definition governs requirements, requirements
govern design, and requirements plus design govern code. It keeps the live
operative surface in the present tense only: once a new current reality is
established, transitional paths are erased from the live product unless
explicitly retained as compatibility features. It treats derived artifacts,
indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views, as read
models, never as constitutional truth. If these claims do not hold, the
work is not spec-driven.

constraints.statement: The method requires full constitutional requirements, code derivable from requirements/design, narrowing at major gates, evidence through scenarios/tests/events/projection/delta, and specification repricing when reality exposes a constitutional gap. Authority stays directional during iteration. Current operative truth is present-tense; obsolete transitions are erased subject to the compatibility exception. Derived artifacts, indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views are read models, never constitutional truth. Failure of these commitments excludes the spec-driven designation. Declarative truth/boundaries over imperative procedure remains a preference.

conditions: Any listed failure holds.

grounding.quote:
The work is not spec-driven if any of these holds (P2, P6):

1. Given goals, a competent team cannot derive a conformant intent surface.
2. Given intent, a competent team cannot derive a conformant
   product-definition surface.
3. Given product definition, a competent team cannot derive conformant
   requirements.
4. Given requirements, a competent team cannot derive a conformant design.
5. Given requirements and design, a competent team cannot derive conformant
   code.
6. A live requirement has no explicit status, category or owning design
   decision.
7. A live requirement has no downstream realisation or explicit deferment
   surface.
8. Code behaviour exists without requirement and design authority.
9. A live domain artifact is rewritten in place after becoming part of the
   live constitutional surface.
10. A capability claim has no operational evidence.
11. Drift is discovered, [Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage)
    locates its cause in the constitutional source, and that source is not
    repriced.
12. A major ambiguity at a constitutional or realisation boundary is neither
    recorded nor explicitly governed.
13. A material product, module, function, application, runtime surface or
    capability has no declared operational lifecycle signal and no recorded
    gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or
    retirement questions.

constraints.statement: Work is not spec-driven if a competent team cannot derive conformant intent from goals, product definition from intent, requirements from product, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; if any live requirement lacks explicit status, category, owning design decision, or both downstream realisation and explicit deferment; if code lacks requirement/design authority; if a live constitutional domain artifact is rewritten in place; if a capability lacks operational evidence; if triage attributes discovered drift to constitutional source that is not repriced; if major boundary ambiguity is neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or if a material product/module/function/application/runtime surface/capability has neither declared lifecycle signal nor recorded gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement questions.
constraints.uncertainty: These are exclusion conditions, not an independently sufficient acceptance test.

grounding.quote:
A failure at any boundary is a specification defect of the upper layer. If
intent cannot be derived from goals, the goals surface is unclear,
contradictory or not concrete enough to orient the next bounded wave of
work. If product cannot be derived from intent, the intent surface is too
vague, contradictory or not concrete enough to guide realisation. If
requirements cannot be derived from product, the product surface is
underspecified, contradictory or not decomposable enough to govern
implementation. If design cannot be derived from requirements, the
requirement surface is underspecified, contradictory or polluted with
accidental implementation detail. If code cannot be derived from
requirements plus design, the design surface is incomplete, ambiguous or
not operational enough. ADRs and design documents are therefore not
decorative explanation; they are the load-bearing bridge between
constitutional truth and executable realisation.

constraints.statement: Specification-drivenness requires ordered reconstructability. Boundary failure is an upper-layer defect: goals unclear/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for the bounded wave; intent vague/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for realisation; product underspecified/contradictory/insufficiently decomposable; requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by accidental implementation detail; or design incomplete/ambiguous/insufficiently operational for code. ADRs/design documents are load-bearing. Sufficiency depends on ambiguity governance; accepted relations may be reused only on exact basis after applicability/invalidation checks. A local selected function's span excludes rebuilding the whole product. The litmus neither waives the design profile's material-change gate nor requires recreation of unchanged accepted views.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed sufficiency, reconstruction-span and design-profile rules are externally owned.

conditions: A real use case, including scenario, deployment or external review, pressures the current model.

grounding.quote:
The generative rule: a real use case (scenario, deployment, external review)
hits the current model; gap analysis identifies what the constitution cannot
express; if the gap is constitutional, not merely a missing implementation,
it re-enters at the layer its [change class](#change-classes) names, and
new goals or intent are written where it changes the work wave, direction
or scope; the repriced surface then flows forward through the layers that
class lists. New intents emerge from repeated, real use-case pressure
against the current model, not from abstract speculation; a gap becomes
intent only once it is concrete. Ad hoc coding pressure does not generate
intent; explicit gap analysis does. This is how the system stays alive
instead of becoming a frozen constitution.

constraints.statement: Explicit gap analysis identifies what the constitution cannot express. A constitutional gap, distinguished from missing implementation, re-enters at its change class's layer and flows forward through that class's layers. New goals/intent arise only where work-wave focus, direction or scope changes; intent emerges from concrete, repeated real-use pressure, not abstract speculation or ad hoc coding pressure. Requirements/design refine cumulatively, code is repeatedly re-derived, and implementation/testing/replay/scenario gaps feed repricing without reversing authority.

exceptions: Optional realisation detail may appear in intent when itself constitutional.
Explicit version labels are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings, or clearly historical/superseded material.

grounding.quote:
Constitutional specification is current-surface law and is written in the
present tense. Dead law does not remain in active constitutional artifacts
for historical comfort: what is no longer live is deleted, superseded or
moved to commentary, and a migration wave does not justify preserving stale
constitutional wording inside the live surface (P3). During a change wave
the live constitutional surface is written in terms of the current truth
and the declared affected boundary; version-line branding such as `2.0` or
`3.0` is not used merely to indicate recency, and explicit version labels
are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings, or clearly
historical or superseded material (§6).

Before a downstream specification artifact is treated as complete, the
whole affected span is checked: is the change class clear; is the re-entry
point lawful for that class; can each downstream layer still be derived
from the upstream layer; do the active intent, product, requirements,
design and qualification surfaces still say the same thing in the affected
scope. If not, the gate is not closed (§4, consistency gate).

constraints.statement: Preserve each layer's role: goals do not replace requirements, intent excludes optional nonconstitutional implementation detail, product is not release notes, requirements carry explicit acceptance and material lifecycle obligations/gaps, and ADRs are not a second requirements surface. Live constitutional wording is present-tense current truth at its declared affected boundary; dead law is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary, even during migration. Recency alone does not justify version branding. Before treating a downstream artifact as complete, check the whole affected span for clear class, lawful re-entry, layer derivability and agreement among active intent/product/requirements/design/qualification; otherwise the gate stays open.

exceptions: Upstream constitutional constraints bind choices; constitutional necessity may require specific filenames, placement, paths or packaging.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state what control or delivery surfaces must exist; design
decides the concrete mechanism that realises them. If a technology stack,
carrier or runtime is not already constrained by an upstream constitutional
surface, choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority
(P2, P1). A tenant's choice of stack, human process or
combination is its execution binding, declared in that design under §11.
The boundary matters especially for
agent-facing bootstrap and control surfaces: requirements may say that
authoritative bootstrap or control surfaces must be present, carry bare
axioms and route to the canonical method; design decides whether those
surfaces are entry documents, embedded blocks, standalone compiled
artifacts or another lawful topology (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12). If
filenames and placement are hardcoded in requirements without
constitutional necessity, the requirement surface has absorbed design
detail and made re-derivation harder.

constraints.statement: Requirements specify required control/delivery surfaces; design chooses mechanisms, including stack/carrier/runtime and tenant execution binding unless upstream already constrains them. Agent-facing requirements may require authoritative bootstrap/control surfaces carrying bare axioms and routing to the canonical method; design chooses entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or other lawful topology. Hardcoding filenames/placement without constitutional necessity absorbs design detail and impairs re-derivation.

conditions: The design profile governs the realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
Non-goals of that profile (P1, P4a): it does not require one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
or replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type. It does require
that the implementation shape remain readable, modular and honest about
where meaning lives and where effects happen. Where a boundary composes
higher-order functions or effectful computation, it does require an
explicit composition and effect algebra with its applicable identity,
closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws (FOUNDATIONS
§4 Composition). The vocabulary is optional; the law is not.

constraints.statement: Semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth, with explicit effects pushed to the edge. Meaning requiring inspection of orchestration, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults indicates excessive imperative coupling. Readability, modularity and honesty about meaning/effects are required. A boundary composing higher-order functions or effectful computation requires explicit composition/effect algebra with applicable identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws.
constraints.uncertainty: The applicable algebra and profile-adoption rule are referenced but not fully supplied.

grounding.quote:
Every inherited or legacy requirement is classified as one of these, and
nothing live remains unclassified (P3):

| Classification | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Deferred | retained in the live surface as an explicit not-yet-operative or not-yet-realised obligation | keep with an honest deferment surface; do not present as current closure |
| Superseded | ownership has moved to a newer constitutional surface or design decision | add Implements and Supersedes to the governing design record |
| Active | remains live constitutional law in the current surface | has an owning design decision; write or update one |
| Orphaned | no longer part of the intended system | remove or explicitly supersede |

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family has explicit header Status and Category; either missing makes it incomplete. All four categories remain constitutional, not priority or user-facing labels. Scenarios validate capability meaning; not every requirement should become a marketed feature. Requirements should avoid premature concrete realisation choices; nonconstitutional path/filename/packaging choices belong to design. Every inherited/legacy requirement is classified: Deferred remains explicitly not-yet-operative/realised with honest deferment and no current-closure claim; Superseded transfers ownership and requires Implements/Supersedes in its governing design record; Active requires an owning design decision to be written/updated; Orphaned is removed or explicitly superseded. Nothing live remains unclassified.

grounding.quote:
The lifecycle statuses (Active, Deferred, Superseded, Orphaned), the
categories and the legacy classifications are declared states of a
requirement, not results, and map to no core value. So are the other
declared classes of this member: the kinds of evidence of §3 (material
advance, prerequisite readiness, preservation, regression), the old-path
classes of §7 Required migration protocol, the inherited-material
classes adopted, superseded, deferred and orphaned and the
implementation classifications `carry_across`, `redundant` and `rewrite`
of §7 Fundamental migration, and the ADR `Status:` values of §10; the change
classes are declared states under §4 Change classes. Each records
a declared classification of its subject, not the answer to a predicate
that an evaluation decides. An evaluation that reads them returns its own
core value with its predicate under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Purpose and material
relation: a declared state is never combined as an evaluation result, so
a requirement marked Active, or evidence classed as material advance,
cannot stand in for a `satisfied` result, and a requirement marked
Deferred or Orphaned cannot stand in for a `falsified` one (P5, P1).

constraints.statement: Requirement lifecycle/category/legacy classifications, evidence kinds, migration old-path classes, inherited-material classes, carry_across/redundant/rewrite, ADR statuses and change classes are declared states with no core-value mapping. They are never combined as evaluation results; evaluations return their own predicate-specific core value. Active/material advance does not mean satisfied; Deferred/Orphaned does not mean falsified.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete core-result algebra is outside the supplied source.

conditions: The project evolves a released predecessor as a successor release.

grounding.quote:
The legacy classification answers one question: what standing an
inherited requirement holds in the project's own live requirement
surface. The disposition of a predecessor claim under
[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
answers another: what a successor release does with a claim of the
released predecessor it evolves, a claim that qualification evaluates.
Where a project's work is also such a successor, each predecessor claim
takes its RELEASE §9 disposition by that section's predicates, and no
lifecycle status or legacy classification supplies or replaces it: a
requirement marked Active may still be `superseded` where its meaning
changed, Superseded names no accepted successor relation, and Orphaned
is not an intentional removal. Purpose and material relation: two
vocabularies with overlapping words would otherwise let a project-level
record stand in for a successor disposition that its owner has not made
(P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Each predecessor claim requires its own RELEASE §9 disposition by that owner's predicates. Project lifecycle, legacy and migration-adoption classifications cannot supply or replace it. Active may coexist with successor superseded if meaning changed; Superseded establishes no accepted successor relation; Orphaned is not intentional removal.
constraints.uncertainty: RELEASE §9 predicates and disposition domain are not supplied.

exceptions: A live requirement may have an explicit honest deferment surface instead of realised design/code/tests.

grounding.quote:
Ownership: every live requirement family maps to one or more owning design
decisions; every ADR or other design record grounds itself in requirements
through an explicit `Implements:` line.

Downstream closure: no live requirement remains a free-floating statement
of intent; if it is live it is realised through the downstream chain or
explicitly deferred with an honest surface that records the deferment, so
every live requirement family has downstream closure, realised in design,
code and tests or explicitly deferred. No shipping code or tests exist as
ungoverned behaviour: behaviour that exists traces back to live
requirements and the design decisions that authorise it. No hidden product
surface is allowed; behaviour without trace authority is accidental law
even if it works.

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family has one or more owning design decisions; every ADR/design record explicitly grounds requirements through Implements:. Live requirements close through design/code/tests or explicit honest deferment. All shipping code/tests trace to live requirements and authorising design; working untraced behaviour is still accidental law. Unowned requirements, ungrounded design, unrecorded deferment and ownerless code are drift; implementation-habit tests lock it in. Persistent event/projection delta is diagnosed by intake among code, requirement/design stack, predictive model or observation. Capability without a scenario has unverified operational meaning. Treating guarantees/governance/verification as features misclassifies them; in-place live-constitution correction corrupts history. A real-use gap inexpressible in requirements re-enters at Requirements or upstream according to class, not by a code hack.

exceptions: Mutable implementation surfaces may be aggressively refactored while they retain that status.
Retained superseded responsibility must satisfy the migration retention relation.

grounding.quote:
Transitional implementation paths, migration
scaffolds and fallback behaviours have no permanent authority in the live
surface: once superseded they are retired, and any retained responsibility
satisfies the retention relation of §7 (closure criterion). The past is
preserved by version control, operational event history where present and
superseded constitutional artifacts. The method does not require shipping
compatibility shims forever, and it does not allow silent mutation of live
constitutional history.

constraints.statement: Published live constitutional domain artifacts cannot be silently mutated in place. An incorrect artifact is superseded by a new version or withdrawn/deleted from the live surface. Superseded transitions, scaffolds and fallbacks retire unless retention is justified; they have no permanent authority and compatibility shims need not ship forever. History is preserved by version control, operational events where present and superseded artifacts.

conditions: Lifecycle aspects materially affect product meaning or an obligation.
exceptions: No implementation mechanism for every phase and no release plan for every requirement is demanded.

grounding.quote:
For product definition this means naming the current product boundary,
intended use context, release and install posture, live-use posture,
observability posture, and retirement or supersession posture where those
materially affect the product's meaning. For requirements it means stating
any invariant obligation that governs build, assurance, release,
deployment, live usage, telemetry, retirement, ownership, source truth,
authority boundary or downstream interpretation; a requirement may defer a
phase only by naming the deferment and the surface that will own its later
resolution.

The rule is an ambiguity detector, not a demand that every requirement
become a release plan. Each phase has one of three answers, and this
section owns them: the phase is answered by the surface; if a phase is
not applicable, the surface says why; if it is unknown, a named gap such
as `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` is recorded.
Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.
[ASSURANCE §16](ASSURANCE.md#16-module-lifecycle-confirmation) applies
the three answers to the design evidence of a governed boundary. When the lifecycle signal is
missing, downstream design may not fill the gap by local convention,
implementation precedent, prompt prose or test fixture; it reprices the
appropriate constitutional surface or carries the ambiguity as explicit,
governed debt (§5).

constraints.statement: Product names boundary, intended use, release/install, live-use, observability and retirement/supersession posture where material. Requirements state invariant build/assurance/release/deployment/use/telemetry/retirement/ownership/source-truth/authority/interpretation obligations. Product/requirements provide enough signal for design or explicitly record ambiguity. Deferral names both deferment and later resolution owner surface. Each phase is answered, reasoned not-applicable, or named unknown; silence is invalid. Missing signal requires constitutional repricing or explicit governed debt, never invention from convention, precedent, prompts or fixtures. These phase answers are declared states, map to no core value and cannot substitute for satisfied; consuming evaluation has its own predicate/result.
constraints.uncertainty: ASSURANCE §16 application and the full result calculus are not supplied.

exceptions: An explicitly product-defined assurance capability may itself constitute product delivery; its evidence still does not author the claim.

grounding.quote:
The exact bound outcome instance stops selecting later product-progress
work when the owning authority accepts it; its witnesses remain regression
and preservation evidence. Acceptance exhausts only that instance and its
declared acceptance interval; it does not discharge an enduring guarantee,
a recurring obligation or a broader product family beyond the accepted
instance. Further work against the accepted instance is preservation, a
named bounded prerequisite for another admitted outcome, or a new change
requiring lawful repricing; it is not additional progress against the
accepted instance (EVALUATION §5).

Selecting the next unresolved outcome already defined by the product is a
goals and work-sequencing decision. Changing an outcome's meaning or scope,
or introducing a new product outcome, requires lawful re-entry at the
product (§4).

Evidence evaluates and constrains its bound product claim. Completion of a
proof surface, matrix, coverage ledger, inventory, design-method artifact,
test suite or other evidence surface cannot by itself select, enlarge or
replace the product outcome. If an assurance capability is explicitly
defined as product behaviour, delivery of that capability is judged as
product progress; its evidence still does not author the claim. The same
artifact may be product output for one claim and evidence for another only
when those roles are declared separately (P6).

constraints.statement: Judge progress and supported-path promotion against the same selected outcome. Only accepted material advance projects product progress; prerequisite readiness names its enabled obligation and remains bounded; preservation/repeated proof and regression are not new progress. Owner acceptance exhausts only the exact instance/interval, not enduring guarantees, recurrence or a broader family; witnesses persist for regression/preservation. Later work is preservation, a bounded prerequisite for another admitted outcome, or lawfully repriced change. Selecting an already-defined unresolved outcome is goals/sequencing; changed meaning/scope or a new outcome re-enters Product. Evidence completion cannot select, enlarge or replace the outcome. One artifact may be output for one claim and evidence for another only with separately declared roles.

grounding.quote:
Admission or renewal of a prerequisite or experiment belongs to the
authority owning the selected work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy,
and is recorded in the existing durable goals or ticket authority. The
admitted basis states its provisional bound and its exhaustion or
falsification condition. Satisfaction of an experiment's stated
decision-discriminating observation exhausts that experiment. Drafting or
validating a ticket or execution contract, retaining active status, or
holding a prior admission cannot create, extend or renew the basis
(ACTIVATION §1, Admission).

Acceptance of the selected outcome, discharge of an admitted prerequisite,
or resolution of an admitted experiment's stated decision exhausts that
basis. A basis or bound also ends when another admitted terminal condition
is reached or it is rejected, withdrawn, superseded, repriced away or
falsified by evidence. Ended authority cannot be renewed by repair,
continuation, evidence, active ticket or run state, or prior admission;
further material work requires a new admission by the owning authority or
its explicitly bounded proxy (P6).

constraints.statement: Prerequisite/experiment authority is only its provisional bound and grants no enlarged outcome, downstream work, promotion, closure or waiver of applicable design/safety/authority/release law. Admission/renewal belongs to the work-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and is recorded in existing durable goals/ticket authority with bound and exhaustion/falsification condition. Experiment observation satisfaction or decision resolution, prerequisite discharge, outcome acceptance, another admitted terminal condition, rejection, withdrawal, supersession, repricing-away or evidential falsification ends the basis. Ticket/contract drafting or validation, active status, repair, continuation, evidence, run state and prior admission cannot create, extend or renew it; further material work needs new owner/proxy admission.

exceptions: Independent work may proceed under its own admitted basis.
Affected-path promotion may resume when regression/gap is repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority.

grounding.quote:
Retention as supported product behaviour, required evidence, regression
protection or bounded donor material confers no further growth authority.
Consumers own deletion, archival, quarantine and salvage mechanics. Salvage
carries only the explicitly re-adopted semantics; it inherits neither the
enclosing work's authority, dependencies or completion claim nor its power
to select further work.

A regression or unresolved gap blocks further promotion on the affected
path until repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority. It does
not globally serialise independent work: parallel work may proceed under
its own admitted basis and cannot be laundered into the governed outcome's
progress claim. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not
complete product or release closure (§6).

constraints.statement: Retention as supported behaviour, evidence, regression protection or bounded donor material grants no growth. Consumers own deletion/archive/quarantine/salvage mechanics; salvage inherits only explicitly re-adopted semantics, not enclosing authority, dependencies, completion or further-work selection. Regression or unresolved gap blocks the affected promotion path, without globally serialising independent authorised work or allowing its progress to be attributed to the governed outcome. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not complete product/release closure.

conditions: A substantive change begins.

grounding.quote:
Every substantive change begins with intake triage, an explicit declared
change intent and a lawful re-entry point into the constitutional chain
(P4b, P2).

constraints.statement: Every substantive change begins with intake triage, explicit declared change intent and lawful constitutional re-entry; the family table traces this route and creates no second decision path.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: F11 attributes ten consequences to premises: owning-layer re-entry rather than report labels; evidence-tested frames rather than names and diagnosis without repair authority; recorded exact-basis classification with distinct fact/judgment/ruling; unknowns withholding only dependent reliance and no assumption of no effect; obligation-conjunction closure rather than events/status; local visible bounded repayable proof deferral without sprint admission authority; recorded ambiguity with risk-policy blocking subject to hard stops; singular acceptance-path authority and downstream projections; shared-contract closure proof with persistent negative break evidence and owned retention; and no inherited authority absent explicit re-adoption. Domain/policy choices remain owned as stated: this member's six classes/four procedures/C-J-O order/material inputs, sprint requirements/triggers, ambiguity distinctions/narrowing, two migration strategies/presumption/old-path classes, inside-out order and implementation classes; project's declared risk policy; adopting profile's escrow suitability; and affected-product human authority's re-adoption selection. Consumers only apply owning rules, adding no decisions.
constraints.uncertainty: The table's foundation standing, external rule definitions and full consumer implementations are references, not independently established here.

grounding.quote:
Triage diagnoses among the four causes of
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),
a defective realisation, an inadequate governing requirement or design, an
inaccurate predictive model, and insufficient observation, and routes each
supported repair to the owner of its cause rather than inferring it from
the intake label; severity and priority follow the policies that
[TICKETS](TICKETS.md) owns; a bug list projects existing work state. This
paragraph applies ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis and states no
second relation (P2, P6).

The frames' results combine under the one
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results): each
keeps the diagnosis it evaluated as its predicate, a counterexample that
one frame finds survives the join, and a frame planned and not applied
leaves its diagnosis open, never ruled out. Counterexample localisation
applies where required (ASSURANCE). This prescribes no reviewer count and no new
review round; required independence stays intact. A diagnosis grants no
repair effects and does not establish that governing meaning must change: a
candidate may instead need correction under sufficient existing law (P6).

constraints.statement: Bug, feature, issue, regression, operator finding, release blocker and scenario failure enter the same triage; no label selects class or bypasses triage for code/tests/release. Evidence selection is S_Δ over I(Δ). Diagnose defective realisation, inadequate requirement/design, inaccurate predictive model or insufficient observation; route supported repair to cause owner, with TICKETS owning severity/priority and bug lists only projecting state. Triangulate the same subject/basis through the smallest sufficient applicable frame configuration, testing each diagnosis against its variables, relations and evidence. Preserve alternatives/uncertainty and identify the smallest lawful repair scope. Failure-exposing frame need not own the cause; renamed duplicate analysis adds no evidence. Conjunction preserves each predicate and any counterexample; unapplied planned frames leave diagnoses open. Required localisation/independence persists without prescribed reviewer count or new round. Diagnosis grants no effects and need not imply changed governing law.
constraints.uncertainty: Frame selection, conjunction, impact-cover calculus, localisation and severity/priority policies are externally owned.

grounding.quote:
Smaller changes may re-enter below Goals only if they explicitly assert
that no upstream constitutional surface is changing. The absence of a
declared change class is process drift. A changed governing relation is
accepted only at its owner; accepting it inside the acting frame is a
violation whatever the size of the delta (ACTIVATION §1).
Triage records the change intent, the class, the re-entry point and when
triage occurred, wherever substantive work begins.
[TICKETS §4](TICKETS.md#change-class) records the class on the carrier.

The change classes are declared states of a change that intake triage
records, not results, and map to no core value. An evaluation that reads
a declared class returns its own core value with its predicate under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A close classification
of [TICKETS §3](TICKETS.md#close-review) that names a layer, such as
`design_reframe`, is a result for its own predicate, mapped there, and
carries the class at which the work re-enters as its domain outcome.
Purpose and material relation: a declared class is never combined as an
evaluation result, so a change classed `realization_refactor` cannot stand
in for a `satisfied` result that no upstream drift occurred (P5, P1).

constraints.statement: goal_reprice changes bounded-wave focus, enters Goals and flows through Intent/Product/Requirements/Design/Code/Evidence only where focus changes deeper truth. intent_reprice changes direction/scope, enters Intent and flows through Product onward. product_reprice changes current product realisation while intent stays stable, enters Product and flows through Requirements onward. requirement_reprice changes constitutional truth while direction stays stable, enters Requirements and flows through Design/Code/Evidence. design_reframe changes structure with intent/requirement truth stable, enters Design then Code/Evidence. realization_refactor changes local code/configuration/attributes without intended constitutional/structural change, enters only realised surface and must prove no upstream drift. Below-Goals entry explicitly asserts no upstream constitutional change. Missing class is process drift; only the governing relation's owner accepts a change regardless of delta size. Record intent/class/re-entry/time wherever substantive work begins. Declared classes are not core results; a ticket close-classification is instead its own predicate result carrying a re-entry class. realization_refactor alone does not prove satisfied no-drift.
constraints.uncertainty: Ticket close-classification mappings are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The explicitly selected source, worksite or qualification capability
produces C over the exact request and desired outcome, the known targets
and effects, the operation grant and work lifetime, the product definition
and governing basis, the baseline and the available candidate, the declared
relations, the accepted design and trace bindings, the evidence and the
applicable rules. Its output identifies the producer and procedure
revision, the inputs, the result, the scope, the source routes, the
reproduction relation, the unknowns and the invalidators. A missing
candidate or missing evidence is an input state, not a claim that nothing
changed.

constraints.statement: An explicitly selected source/worksite/qualification capability produces C from exact request/outcome, targets/effects, grant/lifetime, product/governing basis, baseline/available candidate, declared relations, accepted design/traces, evidence and rules. Output identifies producer/procedure revision, inputs/result/scope/source routes/reproduction relation/unknowns/invalidators. Missing candidate/evidence is not no-change. Expose in order: (1) authority traversal over explicit source/ownership/dependency/composition/projection declarations, reached owners/layers/exact bases, changed/unchanged/unknown relations, edges/frontier, including root/authority/grant changes despite equal public bytes; absent edges prove no irrelevance and uncertain materiality remains J; (2) full relevant serialised-member universe under owning declaration/projection, helpers/generated dependencies, additions/removals and every retained changed typed value/byte with exact before/after; rename is removal/addition unless owner supplies identity preservation, while missing candidate, incomplete enumeration, ambiguous identity or unavailable projection leaves affected delta unknown and membership equality proves no value equality; (3) changed bytes/relations joined to explicit accepted scope/traces/evidence, distinguishing covered/missing/stale/ambiguous/outside-scope, with filenames/listing/digest insufficient and semantic sufficiency remaining J; (4) only declared rules with sufficient facts, recording owners/predicates/consequences, smallest lawful re-entry/next action/evidence or assessment/reserved ruling/carrier lifetime, retaining conflicts/missing premises unresolved. Labels/filenames do not choose routes; settled rules require no invented J.
constraints.uncertainty: These are described operations, not traversals or computations performed by this interpretation.

exceptions: A sufficient existing contract permits candidate rejection or local repair within its grant instead of changing governing meaning.

grounding.quote:
A public delta or other nonconformance does not itself require changing
the governing contract. If that contract remains sufficient for the
authorised outcome, the candidate is rejected or locally repaired within
its grant. The actual governing owner is re-entered when the explicitly
selected desired outcome requires changed meaning or an applicable
assessment establishes governing insufficiency. C determines that
consequence only from sufficient declared premises; unresolved intended
